transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I keep fixating on this small uneven spot around my nose and cheek. It shows up to me in photos, and under the lights at work, and… even when people say they don’t notice it, I feel like it’s the first thing customers or managers see.
How much distress or difficulty does this concern about your nose and cheek cause you in your daily life?

It’s… not like I can’t function, but it is starting to cause problems. My manager noticed I’ve been coming back from breaks late and kind of moving slower at the register. I’m worried it makes me look unreliable, especially because I’m trying to get promoted.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, touching your face, or trying to cover it up, because of how you feel about that spot?

Yeah… I do check it. Mostly on my breaks, in the bathroom mirror. I’ll kind of fix my hair around it, or look at it from different angles.

And I compare myself to girls who come through my line sometimes. I don’t really mean to, but… yeah. Sometimes I take too long and end up late getting back to the register.
How much time do you spend thinking about that uneven spot on your nose and cheek throughout the day?

I don’t know exactly… it’s kind of on and off. But I get stuck on it a lot, especially if I see myself in a photo or under the store lights. Then it’s hard not to think everyone’s noticing it, even when they say they don’t.

When you're concerned about how that uneven spot looks, do you do anything else besides checking the mirror or adjusting your hair — like seeking reassurance from others, measuring the spot, or trying to mentally fix it?

Mostly just the mirror thing… and fixing my hair around it. I don’t really measure it or anything.

I guess I also compare myself to girls who come through my line, like their face looks normal and mine doesn’t. Sometimes I get stuck doing that or checking on my break, and then I’m late getting back.

Do you worry about other things besides that spot when you're around other people, like how the rest of your face or body looks, or do you feel nervous about being judged for other reasons when you're in social situations?

Not really other reasons… it’s mostly that spot. Like around my nose and cheek.

I know it’s probably small, but in photos or under the store lights it feels really obvious. Even when people say they don’t see it, I feel like customers or my managers notice that first.
Have you ever avoided going to work, social events, or other situations because you felt too self-conscious about that spot on your nose and cheek?

I haven’t really skipped work or anything… but it does mess with work some.

Like, my manager’s noticed I come back late from breaks, and I’m slower at the register sometimes. I’m worried it makes me look unreliable, especially because I’m trying to get promoted.
When you're around others, do you think people are actually noticing or talking about that spot on your nose and cheek, or is it more that you're worried they might be?

I guess… I don’t know that they’re talking about it. It’s more that it feels like they notice it right away.

Even if someone says they don’t see anything, under the store lights or in photos it just looks really obvious to me. Like customers or my managers would see that first.
Do you ever feel so upset or distracted by how that spot looks that it interferes with your ability to focus or feel comfortable during the day?

Yeah… sometimes. Mostly at work.

I’ll get distracted checking it, and then I’m late coming back from breaks or I’m slower at the register. My manager’s noticed, I think, and I’m worried it makes me look unreliable… especially because I’m trying to get promoted.
Do you find yourself doing certain things over and over again, like checking the spot in different lighting or trying to mentally fix how it looks, because it bothers you so much?

Yeah… I do that.

On breaks I’ll check it in the bathroom mirror, sometimes from different angles, and I’ll mess with my hair to try to cover it more. I also kind of compare myself to girls who come through my line, which feels embarrassing to say. Sometimes I take too long and end up late getting back to the register.

Besides checking your face in the mirror, adjusting your hair, and comparing yourself to others, do you do anything else repeatedly—like skin picking, applying makeup in a specific way, or going over how you looked in your mind—to try to deal with your concerns about that spot?

Not really anything else… I mean, it’s mostly what I said.

On breaks I check it in the bathroom mirror, fix my hair around it, and compare myself to girls who come through my line. Sometimes I take too long and get back to the register late.
If you knew for certain that no one else could see that spot on your face or notice it at all, would it still bother you?

I think… yeah, it probably would still bother me.

Like, even when people say they don’t see it, I still get stuck on it. Especially in photos or under the store lights, around my nose and cheek. It just feels really obvious to me.

Is it mainly the idea of that specific spot on your nose and cheek being uneven that bothers you, or is it more the fear that others are judging your overall appearance when you're in social situations?

It’s mostly that specific spot… around my nose and cheek. Like it looks uneven to me.

But then when I’m at work, I start thinking it’s what customers or managers notice first, even if people say they can’t really see it.

When you’re looking at that spot on your nose and cheek, do you feel like it’s a defect that makes you physically unattractive, or is it more that you’re worried people will judge or think negatively about you because of it?

It’s… kind of both, I guess. Mostly it feels like that spot makes my face look uneven and unattractive.

But then at work, under the store lights, I start feeling like it’s the first thing customers or managers notice, even if people tell me they don’t see it.

Do you feel that the time you spend thinking about or checking that spot on your face, or the distress it causes you, significantly interferes with your work, relationships, or other important parts of your life?

Yeah… a little. I don’t really like admitting that.

My manager has noticed I come back from breaks late sometimes, and I’m slower at the register. I’m worried it makes me look unreliable, especially because I’m trying to get promoted.
